questions.prompt: Explain why reserving stock for a multi-product cart needs one transaction, and why a transaction alone does not settle the last-unit race.

keyPoints.text: Stating invariants first beats starting from controller names: stock cannot go negative, a pending order restores at most once.
keyPoints.quote: Writing these conditions first is more useful than starting with controller names.

keyPoints.text: If each reservation committed separately, a failed second item would leave the first product short with no order.
keyPoints.quote: the customer receives no order while the first product loses stock

keyPoints.text: Reservation and order creation run in one interactive transaction, so an exception restores earlier writes.
keyPoints.quote: An exception aborts the transaction, restoring earlier writes.

keyPoints.text: A transaction does not automatically settle every race: two requests can both read stock 1.
keyPoints.quote: A transaction does not automatically settle every race.

keyPoints.text: The conditional update makes the database evaluate the condition at the write boundary; a JavaScript if alone gives no guarantee.
keyPoints.quote: The database evaluates the condition at the write boundary.

keyPoints.text: The reservation is a single conditional updateMany per line.

questions.prompt: Walk through the last-unit race table: what each transaction sees, where the guarantee actually lives, and what the loser receives.

keyPoints.text: Both transactions read stock 1 at version 3 and both pass the JavaScript check.
The JavaScript comparison is only a courtesy check for a friendly message.
keyPoints.quote: the JavaScript comparison is a *courtesy check*

keyPoints.text: It is worthless as a guarantee because both requests pass it.
keyPoints.quote: it is worthless as a guarantee because both requests pass it

keyPoints.text: The guarantee is the where clause evaluated by PostgreSQL inside the write.
Stock never goes below zero, no unit is sold twice, and the loser gets a 409.
keyPoints.quote: the loser gets 409 rather than a corrupted row

questions.prompt: Explain the product-editing, money and lifecycle rules, and the limits the guide admits.

keyPoints.text: An unconditional full update from a stale editor would restore consumed inventory, so PATCH carries the expected version.
keyPoints.quote: Sending an unconditional full update would restore consumed inventory.

keyPoints.text: On conflict the UI keeps the draft but does not quietly attach the newer version to old stock.
keyPoints.quote: It does not quietly attach version `5` to old stock

keyPoints.text: Prices cross HTTP as decimal strings and Prisma Decimal avoids floating-point accumulation.
keyPoints.quote: Prisma Decimal calculates totals without binary floating-point accumulation.

keyPoints.text: Order items store the catalog name and price so renaming a product does not rewrite past purchases.
keyPoints.quote: OrderItem stores the catalog name and price at creation

keyPoints.text: Cancellation's conditional status update gives concurrent cancellations one winner.
keyPoints.quote: Its conditional status update ensures concurrent cancellation requests have one winner.

keyPoints.text: A retried successful POST can create a second order because idempotency is not implemented.
keyPoints.quote: A retried successful POST can create a second order

keyPoints.text: Customer references are caller-controlled, so transactions do not establish authorization.
keyPoints.quote: Customer references are caller-controlled, so transactions do not establish authorization.
